definition.def: If something reinforces a feeling, situation, or process, it makes it stronger or more intense.
examples: A stronger European Parliament would, they fear, only reinforce the power of the larger countries. [VERB noun]
This sense of privilege tends to be reinforced by the outside world. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If something reinforces an idea or point of view, it provides more evidence or support for it.
examples: The delegation hopes to reinforce the idea that human rights are not purely internal matters. [VERB noun]

definition.def: To reinforce an object means to make it stronger or harder.
examples: Eventually, they had to reinforce the walls with exterior beams. [VERB noun + with]

definition.def: To reinforce an army or a police force means to make it stronger by increasing its size or providing it with more weapons. To reinforce a position or place means to make it stronger by sending more soldiers or weapons.
examples: Both sides have been reinforcing their positions after yesterday's fierce fighting. [VERB noun]
Troops and police have been reinforced in the city. [VERB noun]

examples.sentence: Such anticipation is constructed and sustained through a variety of non-tourist practices such as films, TV literature, magazines records and videos which construct and reinforce this daydreaming.
They discovered that it helps reinforce the bonds between prairie voles, which mate for life, and triggers the motherly behaviour that sheep show towards their newborn lambs.

Cheeseman also notes another advantage: concrete and steel have similar thermal expansion properties, so steel can be used to reinforce concrete, making it far stronger and more flexible as a building material than it could be on its own.
To reward factors other than performance will only reinforce those other factors.
